findings.issue_text: [BUG] The test's cleanup registration fetches the identity provider by the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so the ResourceClosedException-safe cleanup never targets any of the 20 created IDPs. testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") returns null for every loop iteration (no IDP with alias "alias" was created), and evaluating the method reference `...get("alias")::remove` on a null result throws NullPointerException at cleanup-registration time, failing the test before any of the cache assertions run; even if the client returned a proxy instead of null, the cleanup would remove nothing and the 20 IDPs would leak between test methods.

[BUG] The new predicate arm dereferences idp.getConfig() with a direct .get() call, but IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() returns the raw config map which is null for models constructed without configuration. Any IdentityProviderModel with a non-null organizationId but a null config (e.g. built from a representation or storage layer that never called setConfig) reaching getForLogin throws NullPointerException inside getLoginPredicate, breaking every caller of getForLogin for the realm, not just the one IDP.

[ADVISORY] The re-population path in getForLogin adds the revisioned query with cache.getCurrentCounter() while the initial population path uses startupRevision, an unexplained divergence from the established pattern used by every other cached query in this class. The merged copy of the list query is pinned to the current counter rather than the session's startup revision, so a maintainer changing revision semantics will update one call site and miss the other; the next change to invalidation/reload logic in this class becomes riskier because the two addRevisioned calls in the same method now disagree on the base revision.

[BUG] The cache key for getForLogin (cacheKeyForLogin) omits organizationId from the key while the ORG_ONLY/ALL fetch modes are keyed by mode alone, so the isInvalid short-circuit path is shared across all organizationIds even though the cached content is per-organization. When cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) is called on the organizationId-miss branch (line 231), any concurrent invalidation or a later different-organization lookup that lands on the isInvalid(cacheKey) branch bypasses the per-searchKey map entirely and hits the delegate, so the multi-organization entries stored inside a single IdentityProviderListQuery are effectively uncacheable under invalidation churn: an org A lookup populating the cache, followed by an org B lookup that invalidates and rewrites the single shared entry, repeatedly thrashes one cache slot that all organizations of the realm contend for.

[BUG] The cleanup registration targets alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") returns null and the ::remove cleanup NPEs (and the created IDPs are never cleaned up). The cleanup callback throws NullPointerException at teardown and the 20 test IDPs leak into TEST_REALM_NAME, breaking subsequent cache-count assertions in this and other tests in the class.

[BUG] The second cleanup registration for the newly created idp-alias-20 also uses the wrong alias "alias", so cleanup NPEs and idp-alias-20 leaks. NullPointerException during test teardown; idp-alias-20 (enabled, not hidden) remains in the realm and corrupts login-IDP counts for later tests.

[ADVISORY] The cache-hit path returns raw IdentityProviderModel objects from getById while the invalid/miss path wraps each result with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so cache hits and misses return differently-shaped models. Any caller depending on the organization-aware wrapper's behavior (e.g., org-scoped alias/config adjustments) gets different objects on a warm cache than on a cold cache, producing render/login-page differences that only appear after the cache warms — exactly the kind of intermittent bug QA cannot reproduce.

[ADVISORY] The new test never exercises the two non-trivial branches of getForLogin: the 'existing cache entry but new searchKey' branch (cache.invalidateObject + new IdentityProviderListQuery with parent, addRevisioned with getCurrentCounter) and the getById-null fallback that registers invalidation and delegates. The multi-searchKey merge logic — the most concurrency-sensitive code in this diff — ships with zero verification; a revision/counter mistake in that branch (it uniquely passes cache.getCurrentCounter() where every other branch passes a loaded revision) would only surface as stale login IDP lists in production under multi-org realms.

[ADVISORY] The test never verifies that removing a login-eligible IDP invalidates the login caches — step 1 deliberately removes only the non-login idp-alias-1, leaving the registerIDPLoginInvalidation call inside remove() untested. If the remove-path invalidation is wrong (e.g., storedIdp fetched from the delegate lacks the config that getLoginPredicate inspects), a deleted broker keeps appearing on the login page until the cache TTL/revision expires, and the test suite gives no signal.

[ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally performs idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) — a remote/DB storage read on every removal even when the cache-miss path previously avoided it — solely to obtain the model for login-cache invalidation, when only the internalId and login-relevant fields are needed. Every IDP deletion pays an extra storage lookup; on hot realms with many broker deletions (bulk admin imports/teardowns) this doubles the storage round-trips for removal, and the fetched model is only used to evaluate the login predicate.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate clause dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard while the adjacent clause guards getOrganizationId() == null, and no test in the diff covers an IDP model with a null config map. Any code path that constructs an IdentityProviderModel without calling setConfig (in-memory models, some importers) and passes it through getLoginPredicate/getForLogin throws NullPointerException, taking down the login page instead of degrading to treating the IDP as non-public.

[ADVISORY] The diff changes the shared getLoginPredicate() so that IDPs linked to an organization without BROKER_PUBLIC=true are excluded from login everywhere, not just in the Infinispan cache. This is a functional behavior change to a core SPI predicate used by every IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementation and all login/broker callers, smuggled into a PR whose stated intent is only caching; anyone (JPA-backed deployments with no cache) relying on org-linked IDPs appearing on the login page gets silently changed behavior with no requirement tracing to it.

[BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while the cache-miss path (line 220) wraps delegate results, so cached and uncached invocations return different model shapes for the same query. The invariant 'cached getForLogin is equivalent to delegate getForLogin' is not enforced: the first login page render after a cache miss returns wrapped organization-aware models, and every subsequent render served from the cache returns unwrapped ones, producing inconsistent behavior (e.g. organization-scoped config/alias display) that flips whenever the cache is invalidated.

[ADVISORY] remove(alias) now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (storedIdp) before the isInvalid check, adding a storage round-trip on every removal even when the cached entry already carries the internalId. The previously-guarded delegate lookup becomes an unconditional DB hit on the remove path; a caller bulk-removing IDPs gets one extra storage query per removal that existed only on the invalid-cache branch before this diff.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds an isEnabled() re-filter to both searchForIdentityProviders branches in the login theme bean, a behavior change to the organization login page that is not part of the stated caching intent. IDPs that reach this bean but are disabled now disappear from the org login page for all deployments (cached or not); this is a separate functional fix riding in a caching PR, so any regression it introduces cannot be bisected to its own change and reviewers of the caching work cannot trace it to a requirement.

[BUG] The cleanup registration uses testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove with the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, and since method references are evaluated eagerly, get("alias") returns null and ::remove dereferences null immediately. testCacheIDPForLogin throws NullPointerException on the very first loop iteration (line ~381), so the new test for the caching behavior never executes and none of the asserted invalidation scenarios are actually verified.

[ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation when the IDP remains a login IDP with an unchanged organizationId, but the login cache entries are per (FetchMode, organizationId) and an update that changes any other login-relevant field without changing predicate status still leaves stale internalId sets untouched. The invariant the new cache promises — 'cached login IDP lists always reflect the current delegate state' — is not enforced for updates that keep login-availability but alter which entries should appear (e.g. predicate-relevant config consumed by LoginFilter sub-predicates whose inputs the diff's two-predicate check does not diff); a user gets a stale cached list until an unrelated invalidation fires.

[ADVISORY] The two cache-population branches pass different revision arguments to addRevisioned — the first-entry branch uses the fixed startupRevision while the add-searchKey branch uses cache.getCurrentCounter() — so a freshly built IdentityProviderListQuery is stamped with a stale revision. If another node registers an invalidation for the login cache key between the delegate fetch and addRevisioned (e.g. an admin disables an IDP during a concurrent login-page render), the newly added entry carries the old startup revision and can be admitted/kept as valid on this node, serving the pre-update IDP list to users logging in; the second branch's use of getCurrentCounter() shows the intended invariant, making this an inconsistency rather than a deliberate choice.

[ADVISORY] The missing-searchKey branch uses cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey), which is a local-only invalidation, while every other mutation path in this class uses realmCache.registerInvalidation, which propagates cluster-wide. In a multi-node cluster, node A adds org-X results to its local query entry while node B retains the old entry lacking org-X; two nodes also race in addRevisioned so the last writer drops the other's searchKey. The system self-heals (a missing searchKey triggers a delegate reload), so this is extra DB load and transient per-node divergence rather than a permanent staleness, but the invalidateObject/registerInvalidation asymmetry means the query object's contents are per-node with no convergence guarantee until the next full invalidation.

[ADVISORY] The cached getForLogin path resolves each cached internal ID via session.identityProviders().getById(id) inside a loop — an N+1 lookup pattern (one cache-get or DB hit per IDP) on the login page hot path. Realms with many login IDPs issue N cache/DB lookups per login-page render where the non-cached path issues one query; the cache converts one DB query into N cache round-trips, so for large IDP counts the 'cache' can be slower than the delegate call it replaces. A batched getAllByIds-style fetch or storing the resolved models would keep the hot path O(1) round-trips.

[ADVISORY] IdentityProviderListQuery accumulates one searchKey-to-ID-set entry per distinct organizationId forever — the per-org results are only pruned when the whole login cache key is invalidated by an IDP create/update/remove, never when an organization is deleted or simply stops being queried. A realm with many organizations (Keycloak explicitly targets org-heavy multi-tenant deployments) grows the cached query object without bound; deleted organizations' ID sets linger as garbage. The same pattern exists for the ORG_ONLY and ALL keys independently, tripling the accumulation.

[ADVISORY] The new clause in getLoginPredicate (orgId != null requires BROKER_PUBLIC) changes getForLogin semantics for every IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementation, not just the cached one, despite the PR being framed as a caching change. Out-of-tree custom storage providers and any caller of getForLogin(ALL, orgId) now silently drop org-linked, non-public brokers from the result; if org members were previously expected to see their organization's private brokers on the org-scoped login page (with visibility decided by the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapper rather than the predicate), this central predicate bake-in removes them from all FetchMode paths including ALL, a domain-behavior change hidden inside a caching PR.

[BUG] The PR silently changes the semantics of the shared SPI predicate getLoginPredicate() to exclude organization-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC set, which alters getForLogin behavior for every storage provider (JPA, map, LDAP), not just the cache. Realms that relied on org-linked, non-public brokers appearing via getForLogin (e.g. after explicit organization selection at login) lose those IDPs from the login page with no feature flag, release note, or explicit acceptance in this 'caching' PR — a behavioral objective change smuggled into a performance change; cached and non-cached deployments also diverge for one deploy cycle.

[BUG] The newly added `idp.isEnabled()` re-filter only on the ORG_ONLY/ALL branches concedes that the underlying getForLogin contract now returns wrapped/enabled-untrusted models, and the comment ('re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped') documents a contract change made unilaterally in this PR. Any other caller of getForLogin besides this freemarker bean (e.g. future login flows, custom extensions relying on the previously guaranteed enabled-only result) silently receives enabled-and-disabled mixed results; the intent 'caching must be transparent' was replaced by 'caching may leak unwrapped models, patch callers individually'.

[BUG] The cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of "idp-alias-" + i, so `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")` returns null and the cleanup lambda throws NPE at teardown. Test teardown aborts with NullPointerException and the 20 created IDPs are never removed, polluting the shared test realm and breaking subsequent tests in the suite; the same copy-paste error is repeated a second time at the idp-alias-20 creation site.

[BUG] The cached path in getForLogin returns identity providers built from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both cache-miss paths (lines 216 and 234) do apply the wrapper, so the organization-aware scoping is silently lost whenever the login IDP list is served from cache. A user hitting the login page gets raw IdentityProviderModel objects on cache hits but organization-scoped wrapped models on misses, so the set of brokers offered for login (including org-scoped behavior of org-linked IDPs) differs run-to-run; any security-relevant filtering the wrapper performs (e.g., restricting which org the broker authenticates against) is bypassed for cached responses, letting users trigger organization-unaware broker flows by repeatedly hitting the cached path.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate clause dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null check, so any IdentityProviderModel with a null config map (config is nullable in IdentityProviderModel) throws NullPointerException inside getLoginPredicate(). In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.create/update/remove, registerIDPLoginInvalidation calls this predicate before the delegate operation, so a create or update of an IDP whose config map is null crashes the write path with a 500 instead of performing the create/update, breaking broker administration for that model.

[ADVISORY] The re-check added to the login-page filter only re-validates idp.isEnabled(), but the login-availability predicate now also depends on HIDE_ON_LOGIN and the BROKER_PUBLIC config, so a wrapped model that was disabled-for-login via hideOnLogin or a non-public org link still passes this filter and is rendered as a login option. If any model wrapping path in the cached provider returns a model whose hideOnLogin or organization-visibility config differs from the underlying stored IDP (the same reason the isEnabled re-check was added), a broker the administrator intended to hide from the login page is offered to unauthenticated users, expanding the attack surface of the anonymous login page.

[ADVISORY] The new getForLogin fallback branch (cache entry exists but getIDPs(searchKey) returns null, triggering invalidateObject + re-addRevisioned with getCurrentCounter) is never exercised by testCacheIDPForLogin, because every query in the test uses a distinct cacheKey per FetchMode with a single searchKey. A regression in this branch — e.g. the suspicious use of cache.getCurrentCounter() instead of startupRevision, or a broken parent-chaining in the new IdentityProviderListQuery constructor — ships green; users querying the same FetchMode with two different organizationIds (the exact scenario the branch exists for) get stale or empty IDP lists on the second org with no test failing.

[ADVISORY] The idp == null fallback in getForLogin (cached internal id resolves to no IDP, registerInvalidation and re-delegate) has no test that triggers it. If this defensive path regresses (e.g. registerInvalidation not actually evicting the entry, or an NPE in the fallback), a stale cache entry pointing at a deleted IDP causes login pages to crash or silently drop providers; the diff's test never deletes an IDP while its id remains in a populated login cache.

[ADVISORY] The create-path invalidation registerIDPLoginInvalidation (and the remove-path invalidation of a login-qualifying IDP) is never tested: testCacheIDPForLogin only creates an IDP with hideOnLogin=true and removes the disabled idp-alias-1, both of which skip invalidation by design. Creating a new login-qualifying IDP or removing an enabled login IDP after the caches are populated serves stale login IDP lists indefinitely; no test would catch registerIDPLoginInvalidation being dropped or its predicate inverted.

[ADVISORY] Scenario 4 conflates two invalidation sources: it updates idp-alias-20's config (BROKER_PUBLIC=true) and links it to the organization in the same step, so the test passes even if the org link via addIdentityProvider alone never invalidates the login caches — the update alone already invalidates. Organization admins linking an existing public broker to an org through the OrganizationProvider API (without an IDP update) get a stale cache where the IDP still appears in REALM_ONLY results / disappears from org results with no failure anywhere in the suite.

[BUG] Both create loops register cleanup against testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") instead of the actual alias "idp-alias-" + i, so getCleanup() holds a reference to a nonexistent (or unintended) IDP resource. The 20 IDPs created by testCacheIDPForLogin are never removed by cleanup; get("alias") returns a resource for a nonexistent alias whose remove() no-ops (or, if a provider with alias 'alias' exists from another test, deletes the wrong IDP), leaking state into subsequent tests in the same realm and breaking count-based assertions.

[ADVISORY] The behavior change adding the isEnabled() re-check filter in searchForIdentityProviders (both branches) has zero test modifications — no test in the diff asserts that a wrapped/disabled IDP is filtered from the login page. If the wrap-by-organization path returns disabled IDPs (the exact bug the filter papers over), or if the filter wrongly drops enabled wrapped IDPs, login pages render wrong broker lists with no failing test; the diff also ships no test for the companion getLoginPredicate change excluding org-linked non-BROKER_PUBLIC providers, so an org-linked broker with BROKER_PUBLIC unset (the exclusion branch itself) is never asserted anywhere.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate leg idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)) dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard and is never tested with a config-null or org-linked-unbrokered model. An IdentityProviderModel with organizationId set and a null config map throws NullPointerException inside getLoginPredicate, which registerIDPLoginInvalidation invokes on every create/update — turning IDP admin operations into 500s; the integration test only creates IDPs via representations that always carry a config map, so this is uncovered.

[BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns IdentityProviderModel objects fetched via session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both the isInvalid path (line ~217) and the stale-id fallback path (line ~246) wrap the delegate's results with that method. For the same request, a cache miss returns organization-aware IDP models (e.g. with organization-linked alias/redirect behavior applied) but a cache hit returns raw unwrapped models, so login pages silently render different provider sets/behavior depending on whether the cache was warm — the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean's later filtering (the diff's own isEnabled re-check exists precisely because wrapping can change state) sees models that were never wrapped.

[BUG] The new predicate clause `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` dereferences getConfig() without a null check, and getLoginPredicate() is invoked on every create/update/remove of an IDP via registerIDPLoginInvalidation/registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate. Any IdentityProviderModel whose config map is null (models built by some storage/importers do not initialize config) throws NPE inside create()/update()/remove() on the cached provider, breaking IDP administration for that provider instead of merely skipping cache invalidation.

[ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (a storage round-trip) even on the branch where the alias cache key is valid and a cached copy was available. Every IDP removal in a cached realm pays an extra un-cached storage read that was previously avoided when cached != null; operators with large IDP sets see slower admin remove operations and more load on external IDP storage (LDAP/custom storage) for a value the cache already holds in that branch.

[ADVISORY] getForLogin keys all organizations' results under a single per-realm/per-mode cache key, so each query for a new organizationId invalidates the whole IdentityProviderListQuery object and rebuilds it via the multi-search merge constructor, growing one query object's search map without bound as distinct orgs are queried. Realms with many organizations see cache churn (invalidate + re-fetch from storage on every first-per-org query) and unbounded growth of the merged query entry, degrading the cache hit rate the PR is meant to provide; a per-org cache key (like the existing cacheKeyOrgId pattern) would avoid both.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate stage calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) with no null guard, and IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() returns the raw config field which is null for models constructed programmatically without setConfig. Any code path that builds an IdentityProviderModel without initializing config (some broker/import flows and programmatic admin code do) and then hits getLoginPredicate() — which this diff now invokes on every create/update/remove in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider — throws NullPointerException, turning IDP CRUD and the login page into a 500 instead of degrading to 'not a login IDP'. The pre-existing predicate stages (isEnabled/hideOnLogin getters) were null-config-safe; this stage is not.

[ADVISORY] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns the models resolved by getById() without re-applying the login predicate, and the compensating re-check added in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), not hideOnLogin or BROKER_PUBLIC. During the cross-node invalidation propagation window (and on any node whose registerInvalidation message is delayed), the cached list serves IDPs that are now hideOnLogin=true or BrokerPublic=false as login options; the bean's isEnabled filter does not catch them, so users see brokers on the login page that the admin just hid. The 'might have been wrapped' comment reveals the authors know the cached path returns differently-filtered data but the re-check is incomplete relative to the predicate the cache was built with. Next change to the predicate silently widens this gap because the filter exists in two hand-maintained places.

[ADVISORY] The branch that handles a cache entry missing the current searchKey calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and then cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) instead of the loaded revision, so the revision guard built into addRevisioned is bypassed by an always-fresh global counter. When two nodes concurrently miss on different searchKeys for the same fetchMode key, each invalidates the shared entry and reinstalls its own query (constructed as child of the entry it saw, not the other node's), so with a delayed invalidation the last writer overwrites the first node's entry; because the counter always wins the revision comparison, out-of-order reinstalls are no longer detected and a node can permanently pin stale searchKey results that the per-IDP null check in the read loop will not catch (the stale IDs still resolve via getById). Cache consumers silently receive login IDP lists that omit IDPs another node just added.

The diff adds a new arm in `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`:
```java
.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))
```
This dereferences `idp.getConfig()` without any null-check. If any `IdentityProviderModel` instance can have a null config map, this will throw `NullPointerException` during `getForLogin(...)` evaluation and can break login-IDP queries. The diff itself doesn’t prove whether `getConfig()` is guaranteed non-null, so the defect depends on that contract.

The diff clearly shows two different revision bases being used within the same method for the same cache key, which is an inconsistency and a maintainability risk if revision semantics change. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation when the IDP remains a login IDP with an unchanged organizationId, but the login cache entries are per (FetchMode, organizationId) and an update that changes any other login-relevant field without changing predicate status still leaves stale internalId sets untouched. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The two cache-population branches pass different revision arguments to addRevisioned — the first-entry branch uses the fixed startupRevision while the add-searchKey branch uses cache.getCurrentCounter() — so a freshly built IdentityProviderListQuery is stamped with a stale revision. If another node registers an invalidation for the login cache key between the delegate fetch and addRevisioned (e.g. an admin disables an IDP during a concurrent login-page render), the newly added entry carries the old startup revision and can be admitted/kept as valid on this node, serving the pre-update IDP list to users logging in; the second branch's use of getCurrentCounter() shows the intended invariant, making this an inconsistency rather than a deliberate choice.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin(...)` cache population logic, the `query == null` branch creates a fresh `IdentityProviderListQuery` and calls `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, while the “add missing searchKey” branch invalidates and then calls `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. Given this code is explicitly dealing with cache revisions (`loaded = cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey)` and revisioned adds), stamping a newly created entry with `startupRevision` in one path but the current counter in another strongly suggests an incorrect revision is being attached in the first path, which can lead to serving stale login IDP lists under concurrent invalidation/updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The missing-searchKey branch uses cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey), which is a local-only invalidation, while every other mutation path in this class uses realmCache.registerInvalidation, which propagates cluster-wide. In a multi-node cluster, node A adds org-X results to its local query entry while node B retains the old entry lacking org-X; two nodes also race in addRevisioned so the last writer drops the other's searchKey. The system self-heals (a missing searchKey triggers a delegate reload), so this is extra DB load and transient per-node divergence rather than a permanent staleness, but the invalidateObject/registerInvalidation asymmetry means the query object's contents are per-node with no convergence guarantee until the next full invalidation.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added getForLogin() caching logic, the branch where a cache entry exists but does not contain the current searchKey does call cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) (local cache operation on RealmCacheManager) before rebuilding and cache.addRevisioned(...). Elsewhere in this class’s mutation/consistency paths for these login caches, invalidation is done via realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKeyForLogin(...)) (e.g., create/update/remove and when an IDP lookup returns null). The diff therefore does introduce/contain an asymmetry in invalidation mechanisms for the same logical cache key, which could plausibly lead to per-node divergence or extra reloads in a cluster, even if it may self-heal on misses. The exact cluster-wide semantics of invalidateObject vs registerInvalidation aren’t shown in the diff, so the impact can’t be proven as a correctness bug from this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cached getForLogin path resolves each cached internal ID via session.identityProviders().getById(id) inside a loop — an N+1 lookup pattern (one cache-get or DB hit per IDP) on the login page hot path. Realms with many login IDPs issue N cache/DB lookups per login-page render where the non-cached path issues one query; the cache converts one DB query into N cache round-trips, so for large IDP counts the 'cache' can be slower than the delegate call it replaces. A batched getAllByIds-style fetch or storing the resolved models would keep the hot path O(1) round-trips.

adjudication.rationale: The new cached implementation of `getForLogin` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` builds a `Set<String> cached` of internal IDs, then resolves each via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` inside a `for (String id : cached)` loop (see `getForLogin` added block). This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/scalability concern, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] IdentityProviderListQuery accumulates one searchKey-to-ID-set entry per distinct organizationId forever — the per-org results are only pruned when the whole login cache key is invalidated by an IDP create/update/remove, never when an organization is deleted or simply stops being queried. A realm with many organizations (Keycloak explicitly targets org-heavy multi-tenant deployments) grows the cached query object without bound; deleted organizations' ID sets linger as garbage. The same pattern exists for the ORG_ONLY and ALL keys independently, tripling the accumulation.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin(FetchMode mode, String organizationId)` cache logic, the cached object is an `IdentityProviderListQuery` stored under `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` and indexed by `searchKey` where `searchKey = organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""` (see `getForLogin`). The only invalidation shown for these keys is via `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(...)` on create/remove and `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(...)` on update, both tied to IDP changes. The diff shows no pruning/eviction of old `searchKey` entries (e.g., when an organization is deleted or simply never queried again), so the finding about unbounded per-org accumulation is a real, diff-grounded cache-growth concern, but it is primarily a scalability/memory/architecture issue rather than an immediate correctness failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The create-path invalidation registerIDPLoginInvalidation (and the remove-path invalidation of a login-qualifying IDP) is never tested: testCacheIDPForLogin only creates an IDP with hideOnLogin=true and removes the disabled idp-alias-1, both of which skip invalidation by design. Creating a new login-qualifying IDP or removing an enabled login IDP after the caches are populated serves stale login IDP lists indefinitely; no test would catch registerIDPLoginInvalidation being dropped or its predicate inverted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new cache invalidation logic for login IDP lists on create/remove (`create()` calls `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(model)` and `remove()` calls `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`). The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` populates login caches, then (1) creates `idp-alias-20` with `hideOnLogin=true` (so it won’t satisfy `getLoginPredicate()`) and removes `idp-alias-1` which was created disabled (`setEnabled((i % 2) == 0)`), and asserts caches remain present—explicitly exercising the “should NOT invalidate” paths. It does not include a scenario where a login-qualifying IDP is created or removed after caches are populated to assert that the caches are invalidated, so dropping/inverting `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` in create/remove would not be caught by this test. This is a specific coverage gap for the newly added invalidation behavior, not a demonstrated functional bug in the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Scenario 4 conflates two invalidation sources: it updates idp-alias-20's config (BROKER_PUBLIC=true) and links it to the organization in the same step, so the test passes even if the org link via addIdentityProvider alone never invalidates the login caches — the update alone already invalidates. Organization admins linking an existing public broker to an org through the OrganizationProvider API (without an IDP update) get a stale cache where the IDP still appears in REALM_ONLY results / disappears from org results with no failure anywhere in the suite.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims Scenario 4 “passes even if the org link alone never invalidates” because the preceding IDP update already invalidates the *login* caches. But the diff shows the opposite: `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated)` explicitly **does not invalidate** when both `getLoginPredicate()` are true and `original.getOrganizationId()` equals `updated.getOrganizationId()` (both `null` in Scenario 4, since the org link happens after the update). Updating only `BROKER_PUBLIC` while `organizationId` stays `null` therefore should not clear the login caches. So Scenario 4 does not conflate invalidation sources in the way described; it would still fail if `addIdentityProvider` didn’t invalidate login caches (assuming no other side effects).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Both create loops register cleanup against testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") instead of the actual alias "idp-alias-" + i, so getCleanup() holds a reference to a nonexistent (or unintended) IDP resource. The 20 IDPs created by testCacheIDPForLogin are never removed by cleanup; get("alias") returns a resource for a nonexistent alias whose remove() no-ops (or, if a provider with alias 'alias' exists from another test, deletes the wrong IDP), leaking state into subsequent tests in the same realm and breaking count-based assertions.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating each IDP with alias `"idp-alias-" + i`, the cleanup registered is `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (same again for `idp-alias-20`). This hardcodes the string "alias" instead of the actual created alias, so the cleanup targets the wrong/nonexistent IDP resource and will not remove the 20 (or 21) created IDPs, potentially leaking state into subsequent tests or deleting an unintended IDP if one with alias "alias" exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The behavior change adding the isEnabled() re-check filter in searchForIdentityProviders (both branches) has zero test modifications — no test in the diff asserts that a wrapped/disabled IDP is filtered from the login page. If the wrap-by-organization path returns disabled IDPs (the exact bug the filter papers over), or if the filter wrongly drops enabled wrapped IDPs, login pages render wrong broker lists with no failing test; the diff also ships no test for the companion getLoginPredicate change excluding org-linked non-BROKER_PUBLIC providers, so an org-linked broker with BROKER_PUBLIC unset (the exclusion branch itself) is never asserted anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new filtering/eligibility logic in two places without directly asserting those behaviors in tests: (1) `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders(...)` now re-checks `idp.isEnabled()` in both branches with the comment “idp might have been wrapped”, but the added test (`OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`) exercises `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` and cache invalidation, not the bean’s `searchForIdentityProviders` behavior or any “wrapped IDP becomes disabled/incorrectly filtered” scenario. (2) `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` adds a new exclusion for org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || ...BROKER_PUBLIC`), but the test only sets `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` for org-linked providers (i>=10) and never asserts that an org-linked provider with `BROKER_PUBLIC` unset/false is excluded. This is a specific test-gap tied to newly introduced logic, not a generic ‘add more tests’ comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new predicate leg idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)) dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null guard and is never tested with a config-null or org-linked-unbrokered model. An IdentityProviderModel with organizationId set and a null config map throws NullPointerException inside getLoginPredicate, which registerIDPLoginInvalidation invokes on every create/update — turning IDP admin operations into 500s; the integration test only creates IDPs via representations that always carry a config map, so this is uncovered.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds a new leg to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`:
`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. This dereferences `idp.getConfig()` without a null check. The same predicate is now invoked during admin operations via `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(...)` and `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(...)` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` (called from `create`, `update`, and `remove`). If an `IdentityProviderModel` instance can exist with a null config map, this will throw an NPE and break those operations. The added integration test only creates IDPs from `IdentityProviderRepresentation`, which commonly initializes a config map, so it would not cover the null-config edge case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns IdentityProviderModel objects fetched via session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both the isInvalid path (line ~217) and the stale-id fallback path (line ~246) wrap the delegate's results with that method. For the same request, a cache miss returns organization-aware IDP models (e.g. with organization-linked alias/redirect behavior applied) but a cache hit returns raw unwrapped models, so login pages silently render different provider sets/behavior depending on whether the cache was warm — the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean's later filtering (the diff's own isEnabled re-check exists precisely because wrapping can change state) sees models that were never wrapped.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the cache-miss path explicitly wraps results: `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`. However, on a cache hit it reconstructs the result set by iterating cached IDs and calling `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns those models directly (`return identityProviders.stream();`) without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. From the diff alone, this makes the method’s behavior inconsistent between cache miss vs. cache hit, and the code/comment in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` (“re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped”) reinforces that wrapping can change observable properties/behavior, so returning unwrapped models on cache hits is a correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new predicate clause `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` dereferences getConfig() without a null check, and getLoginPredicate() is invoked on every create/update/remove of an IDP via registerIDPLoginInvalidation/registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate. Any IdentityProviderModel whose config map is null (models built by some storage/importers do not initialize config) throws NPE inside create()/update()/remove() on the cached provider, breaking IDP administration for that provider instead of merely skipping cache invalidation.

adjudication.rationale: In `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` the new clause `Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` dereferences `idp.getConfig()` without a null check. The same predicate is now invoked during `create()`, `update()`, and `remove()` via `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(...)` / `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(...)` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`, so any `IdentityProviderModel` instance with a null config map would trigger an NPE during admin operations rather than simply skipping invalidation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (a storage round-trip) even on the branch where the alias cache key is valid and a cached copy was available. Every IDP removal in a cached realm pays an extra un-cached storage read that was previously avoided when cached != null; operators with large IDP sets see slower admin remove operations and more load on external IDP storage (LDAP/custom storage) for a value the cache already holds in that branch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes remove(String alias) to always execute `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. Previously, the delegate lookup only happened in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch (and the valid-cache branch could use `CachedIdentityProvider` without hitting storage when `cached != null`). This introduces an extra storage/provider round-trip on every removal even when the alias cache entry is present and sufficient, which is a concrete performance/load concern but not a functional correctness bug per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getForLogin keys all organizations' results under a single per-realm/per-mode cache key, so each query for a new organizationId invalidates the whole IdentityProviderListQuery object and rebuilds it via the multi-search merge constructor, growing one query object's search map without bound as distinct orgs are queried. Realms with many organizations see cache churn (invalidate + re-fetch from storage on every first-per-org query) and unbounded growth of the merged query entry, degrading the cache hit rate the PR is meant to provide; a per-org cache key (like the existing cacheKeyOrgId pattern) would avoid both.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s new `getForLogin` caches results under `cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode)`, which is per-realm/per-mode only (`realmId + ".idp.login." + fetchMode`) and does not include `organizationId`. The method then uses `searchKey = organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""` and, when a previously unseen `searchKey` is requested, it calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and rebuilds a new `IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)` that appears to merge prior query state into the new object. This matches the finding’s concern: first-time queries for new orgIds cause invalidation/reload and the stored query can accumulate entries for many distinct orgIds with no bound shown in the diff. This is a concrete performance/architecture issue evidenced by the code, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new predicate stage calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) with no null guard, and IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() returns the raw config field which is null for models constructed programmatically without setConfig. Any code path that builds an IdentityProviderModel without initializing config (some broker/import flows and programmatic admin code do) and then hits getLoginPredicate() — which this diff now invokes on every create/update/remove in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider — throws NullPointerException, turning IDP CRUD and the login page into a 500 instead of degrading to 'not a login IDP'. The pre-existing predicate stages (isEnabled/hideOnLogin getters) were null-config-safe; this stage is not.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new stage to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` that directly calls `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` without checking whether `getConfig()` is null. The diff also newly calls `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` during IDP create/update/remove invalidation (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation*`). However, the claim that `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` can be null in real code paths is not verifiable from this diff alone, so the NPE/500 outcome is plausible but not provably introduced here. The concrete, diff-grounded issue is missing null-guard/defensive handling for `getConfig()` in the predicate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns the models resolved by getById() without re-applying the login predicate, and the compensating re-check added in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), not hideOnLogin or BROKER_PUBLIC. During the cross-node invalidation propagation window (and on any node whose registerInvalidation message is delayed), the cached list serves IDPs that are now hideOnLogin=true or BrokerPublic=false as login options; the bean's isEnabled filter does not catch them, so users see brokers on the login page that the admin just hid. The 'might have been wrapped' comment reveals the authors know the cached path returns differently-filtered data but the re-check is incomplete relative to the predicate the cache was built with. Next change to the predicate silently widens this gap because the filter exists in two hand-maintained places.

adjudication.rationale: In the new cached path of `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin`, the code returns IDPs by resolving cached internal IDs via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and adds them to the result without re-applying the login predicate (`getLoginPredicate()`), e.g. no check for `hideOnLogin`, `isEnabled`, or the new `BROKER_PUBLIC` condition. If an IDP’s properties change so it no longer qualifies for login but a node still has a stale cached ID set (e.g., cross-node invalidation delay), the method will still return that IDP. The compensating change in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` only re-checks `idp.isEnabled()` and therefore would not filter out `hideOnLogin=true` or `BROKER_PUBLIC=false` cases, matching the finding’s concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The branch that handles a cache entry missing the current searchKey calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and then cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) instead of the loaded revision, so the revision guard built into addRevisioned is bypassed by an always-fresh global counter. When two nodes concurrently miss on different searchKeys for the same fetchMode key, each invalidates the shared entry and reinstalls its own query (constructed as child of the entry it saw, not the other node's), so with a delayed invalidation the last writer overwrites the first node's entry; because the counter always wins the revision comparison, out-of-order reinstalls are no longer detected and a node can permanently pin stale searchKey results that the per-IDP null check in the read loop will not catch (the stale IDs still resolve via getById). Cache consumers silently receive login IDP lists that omit IDPs another node just added.

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), when an IdentityProviderListQuery exists but lacks the current searchKey, the code does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` then rebuilds `query` and calls `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())` (not the `loaded` revision it just read via `cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey)`). This inconsistency is directly visible in the diff and could undermine whatever revision-based protection addRevisioned is intended to provide under concurrent updates for the same cacheKey. However, the diff alone does not show addRevisioned’s semantics or cluster invalidation behavior, so the specific “permanent stale pinning” outcome can’t be conclusively verified from the PR.
